body.method: Maximum entropy with a Sharpe floor

violations.message: ex-ante tracking error 6.24% exceeds the 6.0% budget vs. 60/40 equity-bond benchmark

body.rationale: The gap is material now. In an expansion regime, CMA return estimates carry real information; max_sharpe's 0.46 against equal weight's 0.36 is a meaningful spread. Still, acting fully on them yields a 3.8-asset portfolio that is highly exposed to estimation error in μ. Meanwhile, the registry's risk-based alternatives to return-chasing are unusable this run, with six of them failing the IPS by concentrating in low-volatility assets. Maximum entropy with a Sharpe floor offers a principled middle path: it uses the CMAs only as far as needed to clear a stated efficiency bar, then spends all remaining freedom on breadth. Breadth limits the damage when the CMAs are wrong. It is also the method the PC-researcher proposed in the paper's March 2026 run, so it has precedent in this pipeline. It is not claimed to be unconditionally better. At the same floor it will by construction give up Sharpe relative to max_sharpe, and its value depends on the CMAs being informative but noisy. global_minimum_variance was rejected because it would most likely reproduce the inverse_variance/hierarchical_risk_parity concentration that is already failing the IPS. mean_downside_risk was rejected because it is a return-optimiser that would likely concentrate much like max_sharpe and cvar_minimization.
body.notes: Proposed method: maximum_entropy (Bera and Park (2008)). Objective: Maximise the Shannon entropy of the long-only weights, -Σ w_i ln w_i (the most spread-out portfolio), subject to the portfolio's CMA-implied Sharpe ratio meeting a floor, full investment, and the IPS constraints including the volatility cap. Gap in the registry: The table shows a breadth-versus-return split that no registry method sets out to resolve. The broad, IPS-compliant portfolios (equal_weight, eff. N 18.0; volatility_targeting, eff. N 17.0) do not use the CMAs and reach Sharpe of only 0.36. Every CMA-driven optimiser concentrates: max_sharpe reaches 0.46 on 3.8 effective assets, black_litterman 0.41 on 6.1, and cvar_minimization 0.33 on 2.9. resampled_efficient_frontier gets 13.3 effective assets at 0.41, but its breadth is a side effect of averaging resampled frontiers, not something it targets or can be tuned to. The risk_structured and tail methods (inverse_volatility, inverse_variance, risk_parity, hierarchical_risk_parity, maximum_diversification, tail_risk_parity) collapse into the same low-volatility assets: eff. N 1.4–7.6, volatility 0.65–3.11%, and all six FAIL the IPS. No method in the registry states the objective 'as diversified as possible in weights, subject to an explicit return-efficiency requirement.' Maximum entropy with a Sharpe floor states it directly and makes the breadth-versus-Sharpe trade-off an explicit parameter. Main weakness: Entropy is measured in weight space, not risk space. Spreading weights evenly can still leave risk dominated by the highest-volatility assets, so a high effective N here can overstate true diversification, the opposite of risk_parity's error. The result also hinges on an arbitrary Sharpe floor. At or below 0.36 the method collapses to equal weight. Near the top of the 0.36–0.46 range it approaches max_sharpe's concentrated portfolio and inherits its sensitivity to errors in the CMA expected returns, because the binding floor makes the weights depend on μ. A practical concern for the vote follows from this: at a mid-range floor, its portfolio may land close to resampled_efficient_frontier and equal_weight. That would add little that is distinct, and the adversarial diversifier's centroid would shift only marginally.
